To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

regular electronic monitoring of peak expiratory flows and asthma symptoms provides a high sensitivity and specificity for detecting severe exacerbations in patients with severe asthma and that the strongest risk factors for severe exacerbations were low asthma control, eosinophilia, obesity and poor health-related quality of life.
electronic diary data are a good tool to monitor asthma control and to identify patients at risk of exacerbations, which is of particular relevance in the current era of precision medicine.
regular electronic monitoring of PFE and asthma symptoms provides a sensitivity and specificity of 65% and 95%, respectively, for the detection of severe exacerbations of asthma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of electronic monitoring to identify exacerbations of asthma.
the detection of exacerbations in patients with asthma based on electronic data.
the development of an electronic monitoring system that is able to detect asthma exacerbations and to provide information for individualized treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of electronic diaries to detect exacerbations in asthma is a promising tool for the future.

the use of electronic monitoring of PPE and asthma symptoms provides a reasonable sensitivity and specificity for detection of exacerbations and may be suitable as a personal internet-based monitoring for asthma control.
a 20% reduction in peak expiratory flows and/or a 20% rise in daytime symptoms over 2 consecutive days is a good indicator of an impending exacerbation in asthma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
electronic monitoring of PFE and asthma symptom is a good method for detecting asthma exacerbations.

the use of an algorithm combining a 2-day 20% decrease of peak expiratory ﬂow (PEF) or 2-day 40% increase of day symptoms was able to detect severe exacerbation of asthma with 65% sensivity and 95% speciﬁcity.
the combination of PEF and day symptoms can be used to predict exacerbation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of PEF and symptom monitoring can be used as a surrogate for exacerbations, and that patients with severe asthma and a low asthma control questionnaire score, a high body mass index, a high sputum eosiphil count, or a low quality of life have a high risk of exacerbation.
electronic diary data are useful for identifying exacerbations in patients with asthma.
electronic monitoring of PPEF and asthma symptoms provides a good detection of asthma exacerbations.
